subject: Solstice Health - Geographic commitment, private-link clauses and operator controls
messages:
From: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@solsticehealth.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: Glen Park <glen.park@solsticehealth.com>, procure@solsticehealth.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Solstice regional commitment + PrivateLink clauses - initial ask

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Solstice is excited about the latency profile and model isolation options. Our legal & security teams are consolidating hosting commitments for vendors this quarter. Two quick asks so we can move this to procurement: 

1) A short, signed letter that confirms Redwood can isolate customer traffic to US-only nodes (no cross-border egress) when we opt into Private deployments. We need the wording to call out: US regions (us-east/us-west), private peering or PrivateLink, and operator access controls.

2) Any clarifying language around PrivateLink/privatedeploy clauses for our T&Cs. Our counsel wants to understand fallback behavior (if a node enters maintenance, what happens to data flow) and who has operator keystore access.

We also have a SIG/CAIQ intake — SOC 2 artifacts will be requested but that’s a separate packet. Can you attach a short runbook and a sample peering diagram?

Goal: get a draft letter + clause redlines by Jan 26 so procurement can prepare a PO.

Best,
Laura
Laura Simmons
Director, Security & Privacy
Solstice Health

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Glen Park <glen.park@solsticehealth.com>, irene.choi@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solstice regional commitment + PrivateLink clauses - initial ask

Hi Laura — appreciate the clear list. Quick replies inline: 

1) We can provide a signed Regional Deployment Commitment letter that states Redwood will only serve Solstice traffic from US regions you specify (us-east-1, us-west-2) when Private deployment is selected. The letter will include our standard fallbacks: automatic routing to a standby US-only pool scoped to your tenancy; no cross-border peering without explicit change request and a signed amendment.

2) Keystore/operator access: our operator keystore split model keeps customer keys in customer-managed KMS when requested (we support customer KMS/HSM integrations). By default the Redwood operator account does not have unencrypted access to your model keys or plaintext content. We will include a short appendix describing HSM/KMS split, operator roles, and SOC 2 controls around access logging.

I attached a short runbook and a sample PrivateLink peering diagram for your team to review. I’ll draft the letter and a redline of the PrivateLink clause and share by Jan 22 to give you time before Jan 26.

Attaching: runbook-private-peering-20260116.pdf

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 07:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Solstice regional commitment + PrivateLink clauses - operator/hsm clarifications

FYI team — forwarding Solstice ask. Avery, thanks for the draft promises. Two technical clarifications procurement will ask that we should pre-answer in the letter and the appendix: 

- Key custody: confirm if they want customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest encryption across model artifacts or only for signing of operator actions. We support both but the wording needs to be explicit.

- Operator access model: add that operator access is role-based, requires 2-person approval for keystore operations, and all sessions are recorded and retained per our SOC 2 retention policy (we should point to the SOC 2 artifact link).

- Maintenance fallback: when we route to standby US-only pool, clarify that cached KV states are invalidated unless they pin snapshot replication. Provide an opt-in checkbox in the letter for replica behavior.

Marissa — can you add the HSM/KMS snippet and Ben, please confirm the SLA/standby pool latency SLA we can guarantee in writing (e.g., < 60ms added tail latency for routed requests within US pool)?

-Irene

From: Glen Park <glen.park@solsticehealth.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solstice regional commitment + PrivateLink clauses - initial ask

Avery / Irene / Marissa — thank you for the quick turnaround and the runbook. We reviewed the drafts internally and have a few redlines: 

1) We need explicit statement that egress to any non-US endpoint is blocked by default and may only be enabled after a formal change request signed by both parties (redline attached).

2) On KMS: Solstice will require customer-managed KMS for all environments that process PHI. Please confirm Redwood supports a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) flow and whether an HSM-backed customer key can be used to wrap the operator keystore.

3) On operator access: we want a statement that operator keystore operations require 2-person approval and that a real-time alert is sent to our SOC channel when such operations occur.

4) Please include a sample DocuSign link for the letter so procurement can route it to our legal team quickly.

Attached: redline_privatelink_clauses_20260125.pdf

If you can get a signed letter plus the redline response by Tue Jan 28 EOD, procurement will get a PO moving that afternoon.

Thanks — Glen
[Attachment: redline_privatelink_clauses_20260125.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@solsticehealth.com>, Glen Park <glen.park@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solstice regional commitment + PrivateLink clauses - signed letter and next steps

Laura / Glen — attaching our signed Regional Deployment Commitment letter and a short appendix that addresses the redlines (BYOK/HSM flow, 2-person operator approvals, alerting to your SOC channel, and explicit US-only egress lock). Highlights: 

- BYOK/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure BYOK) and can configure keys so that customer HSM-wrapped keys are used to encrypt operator keystore data. Appendix explains the wrap/unwrap flow and that Redwood never holds unencrypted customer keys.

- Egress lock: We will enable a tenancy-scoped policy that blocks routing to non-US regions for Solstice by default. Any change requires a formal change request and counter-signed amendment.

- Operator approvals & monitoring: operator keystore operations require two authorized engineer approvals and generate an immediate audit entry; we will send event hooks to your SOC webhook, and the operation is retained for 365 days as part of our SOC 2 evidence package.

- Maintenance fallback: standby US-only pool will be used. We documented optional snapshot replication for KV cache; if you opt-in replication is active and we commit to preserving session states across failovers.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/r/redwood-solstice-region (sample envelope - will replace with final upon your PO)

Attachments: Regional_Deployment_Commitment_Solstice_20260128.pdf, appendix-byok-hsm-operator-20260128.pdf

Next steps: Once you confirm the DocuSign envelope and the PO trickles through, legal will finalize the amendment. Procurement, let us know if you need a specific format for your purchasing system and we’ll push the signed copy to your HubSpot record HS-32874.

Thanks everyone — cc’ing Irene/Marissa/Ben for records.

Best,
Avery
